es: Seguir conversaciones rápidas con voces que se solapan, frases que se quedan a medias y cambios bruscos de turno, y reconstruir la idea de cada hablante sin perder el hilo.

vocabulary.es: lograr decir algo (cuando otro no para)

teaching.en: When excited friends overlap, sentences trail off halfway and the listener has to rebuild the meaning from whatever is left.
teaching.es: Cuando unos amigos entusiasmados se solapan, las frases se quedan a medias y el oyente tiene que reconstruir el significado con lo que queda.
teaching.explanationEs: Overlap describe voces que suenan a la vez; trail off, una frase que se apaga sin terminar.
segments: When excited friends overlap, sentences trail off halfway and the
listener has to rebuild the meaning from whatever is left.
teaching.audioText: When excited friends overlap, sentences trail off halfway and the listener has to rebuild the meaning from whatever is left.

teaching.en: Hang on, sorry to interrupt, but I thought the meeting had been moved to Friday, not to Thursday.
teaching.es: Espera, perdona que interrumpa, pero pensaba que la reunión se había pasado al viernes, no al jueves.
teaching.explanationEs: Hang on frena la conversación; sorry to interrupt pide permiso para cortar.
segments: Hang on, sorry to interrupt, but I thought the
meeting had been moved to Friday, not to Thursday.
teaching.audioText: Hang on, sorry to interrupt, but I thought the meeting had been moved to Friday, not to Thursday.

teaching.en: We all talk over each other and interrupt constantly, so I sometimes lose the thread of what anyone is saying.
teaching.es: Todos hablamos encima unos de otros y nos interrumpimos sin parar, así que a veces pierdo el hilo de lo que dice cada uno.
teaching.explanationEs: Lose the thread = perder el hilo; talk over each other = hablar a la vez.
segments: We all talk over each other and interrupt constantly, so
I sometimes lose the thread of what anyone is saying.
teaching.audioText: We all talk over each other and interrupt constantly, so I sometimes lose the thread of what anyone is saying.

teaching.en: Whenever Tom is on a roll, nobody can get a word in edgeways, so we chime in early and our voices overlap.
teaching.es: Cuando Tom está lanzado, nadie logra meter una palabra, así que intervenimos pronto y nuestras voces se solapan.
teaching.explanationEs: Get a word in edgeways = lograr decir algo cuando otro no para; chime in = intervenir de forma espontánea.
segments: Whenever Tom is on a roll, nobody can get a word
in edgeways, so we chime in early and our voices overlap.
teaching.audioText: Whenever Tom is on a roll, nobody can get a word in edgeways, so we chime in early and our voices overlap.

teaching.en: Anyway, as I was saying, let us switch to the budget before the room gets too noisy to hear properly.
teaching.es: En fin, como iba diciendo, pasemos al presupuesto antes de que la sala se ponga demasiado ruidosa para oír bien.
teaching.explanationEs: As I was saying retoma lo dicho antes; switch to + tema cambia de tema a propósito.
segments: Anyway, as I was saying, let us switch to the
budget before the room gets too noisy to hear properly.
teaching.audioText: Anyway, as I was saying, let us switch to the budget before the room gets too noisy to hear properly.

teaching.en: Sorry, did I cut in? Go ahead; I did not mean to interrupt, I simply got carried away.
teaching.es: Perdona, ¿me metí en medio? Adelante; no quería interrumpir, simplemente me dejé llevar.
teaching.explanationEs: Go ahead devuelve el turno a quien fue interrumpido; cut in = meterse a mitad de una frase ajena.
segments: Sorry, did I cut in? Go ahead; I did
not mean to interrupt, I simply got carried away.
teaching.audioText: Sorry, did I cut in? Go ahead; I did not mean to interrupt, I simply got carried away.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple «hang on» en esta escena?

choices.text: It invites Tom to carry on with the rest of his explanation.
It changes the subject to the invitation itself.
It stops the talk so that she can check something.

feedback.es: Hang on frena a Tom para comprobar un dato; no le cede el turno (eso sería go ahead) ni cambia de tema.

hint.es: Es una fórmula para frenar, no para seguir.

origin.text: Tom was halfway through giving the schedule when Mia said hang on, because the date he had just read out did not match the one on the invitation.

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdona, no quería interrumpir; adelante, por favor.»

feedback.es: Go ahead es la fórmula para devolver el turno a quien se interrumpió.

hint.es: Verbo de movimiento de dos letras.

origin.text: Sorry, I did not mean to interrupt you. Please ___ ahead; I would like to hear the rest of your idea.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con la función que cumple en la conversación.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula gestiona el turno de una manera distinta: frenar, ceder, retomar o pedir permiso.

hint.es: Piensa en si la fórmula quita o da la palabra.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo reacciona Leo cuando Ana habla por encima de él.

choices.text: He waits and then returns to his own point.
He asks Ana to say the time again so that he can check it.
He repeats the time more loudly until she agrees.

feedback.es: Leo no discute ni pide aclaraciones: espera y retoma su idea justo donde la había dejado.

origin.audio: Leo started to say that the train left at nine, but Ana, talking over him, insisted that it was ten past. Leo did not argue. He simply waited, then picked up where he had stopped and said that the platform had changed.

prompt.es: ¿Qué deduces de la última frase de Tom?

choices.text: That he would now rather go to one of the other parties.
That he had kept Friday free because he thought the party was then.
That he had turned down the invitations because Mia asked him to.

feedback.es: Tom rechazó otras invitaciones para el viernes porque creía que la fiesta era ese día; su frase anterior, cortada por Sara, iba en esa dirección.

origin.text: Tom: Are you coming on Friday or— Mia: Saturday, I told you Saturday. Tom: Sorry, hang on, I thought the party was— Sara: Saturday. Everybody knows it is Saturday. Tom: Then I have already turned down two other invitations for Friday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Pierdo el hilo cuando todos hablan encima de los demás.»

answer.text: I lose the thread when everyone talks over each other

feedback.es: When + sujeto + verbo explica cuándo ocurre: talk over each other describe el solapamiento.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dato de Sara cambiaba los planes de la fiesta.

choices.text: The cake could not be ordered before Thursday.
Carlos could pay only at the end of the month.
The flat would not be free until Saturday.

feedback.es: El dato de Sara es la fecha del departamento (sábado, no viernes); el pedido del pastel es de Mia y el pago de Carlos.

origin.audio: Four flatmates were planning a surprise party, and nobody finished a sentence. Mia started to say that the cake should be ordered by Thursday, but Tom cut in to ask who was paying, and Carlos, talking over both of them, said he could pay if nobody minded waiting until the end of the month. Sara tried to get a word in edgeways, because the flat would be free only on Saturday, not on Friday, which changed everything. Mia laughed, said hang on, as she was saying, the cake came first, and asked Sara to go ahead. Sara repeated the date, and everyone agreed, although Carlos was still not sure about the money.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la reacción final de Carlos.

choices.text: That the question of the money was still open.
That he could not attend the party on Saturday.
That he preferred to leave the planning to the others.

feedback.es: «Still not sure about the money» indica que para él el tema del dinero seguía pendiente, aunque aceptó la fecha.

origin.audio: Four flatmates were planning a surprise party, and nobody finished a sentence. Mia started to say that the cake should be ordered by Thursday, but Tom cut in to ask who was paying, and Carlos, talking over both of them, said he could pay if nobody minded waiting until the end of the month. Sara tried to get a word in edgeways, because the flat would be free only on Saturday, not on Friday, which changed everything. Mia laughed, said hang on, as she was saying, the cake came first, and asked Sara to go ahead. Sara repeated the date, and everyone agreed, although Carlos was still not sure about the money.

prompt.es: Completa: «Perdona, ¿me metí en medio justo cuando ibas a explicarlo?»

feedback.es: Cut in (o chime in, jump in) describe meterse en una frase ajena antes de que termine.

origin.text: Sorry, did I ___ in just as you were about to explain? Please, go ahead; I will wait for you to finish.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como iba diciendo, nadie había reservado la sala para el viernes.»

answer.text: As I was saying nobody had booked the room for Friday

feedback.es: As I was saying retoma lo dicho antes; el resto da el contenido con el pasado perfecto had booked.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender esta pauta de reacciones?

choices.text: That they had all agreed earlier who would do it.
That none of them wanted to take on that job.
That they had not heard Sara's question over the noise.

feedback.es: Nadie responde: cambian de tema, se excusan y siguen con otra cosa, señal de que evitan la tarea de contárselo a Leo; no hay acuerdo previo ni problema de ruido.

origin.text: Sara asked who was going to tell Leo that his proposal had been turned down. Nobody said no. Carlos changed the subject, Mia suddenly remembered an appointment, and Tom carried on talking about the menu as if the question had never been asked.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace Sara después de que todos se ríen.

choices.text: She laughs along and drops the subject.
She asks Leo to start the explanation again.
She goes back to explaining the new rota.

feedback.es: Sara espera y retoma su explicación con «as I was saying».

origin.audio: Sara was about to explain the new rota when Leo chimed in with a joke about the office coffee, and three people laughed at once. Sara waited, smiled and said, as I was saying, the rota starts on Monday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Con tanto ruido, perdí el hilo de la conversación.»

feedback.es: Lose the thread es la colocación para perder el hilo de lo que se está diciendo.

origin.text: The restaurant was so noisy that everybody spoke at once, and halfway through dinner I lost the ___ of the conversation completely.

es: Comprender a hablantes de India, Nigeria, Irlanda y Australia reconociendo rasgos de léxico y gramática propios de cada variedad del inglés, y captar la idea general sin descifrar cada palabra.

vocabulary.es: dar un toque de llamada (inglés de Nigeria)

teaching.en: Because a regional variety is a full system, not a mistake, colloquial words such as arvo or heaps are perfectly normal there.
teaching.es: Como una variedad regional es un sistema completo y no un error, palabras coloquiales como arvo o heaps son perfectamente normales allí.
teaching.explanationEs: Colloquial = propio del habla cotidiana; arvo (tarde) y heaps (un montón) son rasgos del inglés australiano.
segments: Because a regional variety is a full system, not a mistake,
colloquial words such as arvo or heaps are perfectly normal there.
teaching.audioText: Because a regional variety is a full system, not a mistake, colloquial words such as arvo or heaps are perfectly normal there.

teaching.en: In India a colleague may ask you to prepone tomorrow's meeting, which means moving it earlier, the opposite of postpone.
teaching.es: En la India un colega puede pedirte que adelantes la reunión de mañana, lo que significa pasarla a una hora más temprana, lo contrario de postpone.
teaching.explanationEs: Prepone es típico del inglés de la India: se forma por analogía con postpone.
segments: In India a colleague may ask you to prepone tomorrow's
meeting, which means moving it earlier, the opposite of postpone.
teaching.audioText: In India a colleague may ask you to prepone tomorrow's meeting, which means moving it earlier, the opposite of postpone.

teaching.en: How far is a friendly greeting in Nigeria, and flash me means ring once and hang up so that I call you back.
teaching.es: How far es un saludo amistoso en Nigeria, y flash me significa llamar una vez y colgar para que yo devuelva la llamada.
teaching.explanationEs: How far? no pregunta por la distancia: equivale a «¿qué tal?»; flash funciona como verbo.
segments: How far is a friendly greeting in Nigeria, and flash me means
ring once and hang up so that I call you back.
teaching.audioText: How far is a friendly greeting in Nigeria, and flash me means ring once and hang up so that I call you back.

teaching.en: An Irish speaker who says I am grand is fine, not big, and I am after finishing means that I have just finished.
teaching.es: Un irlandés que dice I am grand está bien, no es grande, y I am after finishing significa que acabo de terminar.
teaching.explanationEs: Grand = estupendo, bien; be after + -ing expresa una acción recién terminada.
segments: An Irish speaker who says I am grand is fine, not big,
and I am after finishing means that I have just finished.
teaching.audioText: An Irish speaker who says I am grand is fine, not big, and I am after finishing means that I have just finished.

teaching.en: An Australian might say I reckon we have heaps of time this arvo, and listeners soon pick up on these words.
teaching.es: Un australiano podría decir Creo que tenemos un montón de tiempo esta tarde, y quien escucha pronto se da cuenta de estas palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: Reckon = creer; pick up on = percibir algo que no se dice de forma explícita.
segments: An Australian might say I reckon we have heaps of time
this arvo, and listeners soon pick up on these words.
teaching.audioText: An Australian might say I reckon we have heaps of time this arvo, and listeners soon pick up on these words.

teaching.en: Colloquial speech in every variety carries a distinctive lilt, and if you get the gist you can manage without every word.
teaching.es: El habla coloquial de cada variedad tiene una cadencia característica, y si captas la idea general puedes arreglártelas sin entender cada palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Get the gist = entender lo esencial; lilt es el ritmo melódico de un acento.
segments: Colloquial speech in every variety carries a distinctive lilt, and if
you get the gist you can manage without every word.
teaching.audioText: Colloquial speech in every variety carries a distinctive lilt, and if you get the gist you can manage without every word.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pide la colega de la India cuando escribe «prepone»?

choices.text: To hold the review earlier than planned.
To cancel the review until further notice.
To move the review to the afternoon.

feedback.es: Prepone es lo contrario de postpone: pasar la reunión a una hora más temprana, como explica el cliente que se une antes del almuerzo.

origin.text: Our colleague in India wrote: Could we prepone tomorrow's review to nine, so that the client can join us before lunch?

prompt.es: Completa: «Estoy bien, gracias; acabo de terminar los exámenes.»

feedback.es: Grand significa «bien, estupendo» en el inglés de Irlanda, no «grande».

hint.es: Una palabra de cinco letras que aquí no significa «big».

origin.text: Asked how she was, the Irish student smiled and said: I am ___, thanks; I am just after finishing my exams.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra con la variedad del inglés en la que es típica.

feedback.es: Cada rasgo pertenece a una variedad: prepone (India), flash (Nigeria), grand (Irlanda) y arvo (Australia).

hint.es: Piensa en una palabra de cada país del texto de la clase.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer Leo al llegar al aeropuerto.

choices.text: Send her a long message.
Ring once and hang up.
Call and wait until she answers.

feedback.es: Flash her significa dar un toque de llamada: ella no puede pagar una llamada larga.

origin.audio: Leo's cousin in Lagos answered the phone with how far, and only afterwards did he realise that it was a greeting, not a question about distance. Later she asked him to flash her when he arrived at the airport, because she could not afford a long call.

prompt.es: ¿Qué dice la vecina irlandesa de Tom sobre sus resultados?

choices.text: She is waiting for them, and feels sure they will be good.
She got them a while ago, and they were better than expected.
She has only just got them, and they are a real disappointment.

feedback.es: I am after getting indica una acción recién terminada: acaba de recibir los resultados, y «not what I expected» muestra que son una decepción.

origin.text: Tom asked his Irish neighbour how the exams went. She said: They were grand, although I am after getting my results and they are not what I expected.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Creo que tendremos un montón de tiempo esta tarde.»

answer.text: I reckon we will have heaps of time this arvo
accepted: I reckon we will have heaps of time this arvo
We will have heaps of time this arvo I reckon

feedback.es: Reckon = creer y heaps of time = un montón de tiempo, dos rasgos coloquiales del inglés australiano.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige para qué prometió Leo «flash» al narrador al llegar.

choices.text: To signal his arrival without paying for a proper call.
To warn him that the meeting would start late.
To confirm that the meeting had been moved earlier.

feedback.es: Flash me significa dar un toque de llamada: Leo avisará de que ha llegado sin gastar saldo en una llamada completa; el retraso y el cambio de hora no se mencionan en relación con flash.

origin.audio: Last month I joined a project with colleagues in four countries, and the first call was a lesson in listening. Ana, in Pune, asked whether we could prepone the next meeting to nine o'clock, and for a moment I thought she meant the opposite. Leo, in Lagos, opened with how far, which is simply hello, and promised to flash me when he arrived, because a proper call would eat up his credit. Mia, in Cork, said that she was grand, just after finishing her exams. Finally Tom, in Perth, reckoned there would be heaps of time this arvo. None of it was difficult once I stopped working out every word and started to get the gist.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el narrador al final sobre cómo seguir una conversación.

choices.text: That colleagues should agree on one standard form before meetings.
That getting the overall sense matters more than working out each word.
That understanding comes only after years living in those countries.

feedback.es: Dice que todo fue fácil cuando dejó de descifrar cada palabra y captó la idea general.

origin.audio: Last month I joined a project with colleagues in four countries, and the first call was a lesson in listening. Ana, in Pune, asked whether we could prepone the next meeting to nine o'clock, and for a moment I thought she meant the opposite. Leo, in Lagos, opened with how far, which is simply hello, and promised to flash me when he arrived, because a proper call would eat up his credit. Mia, in Cork, said that she was grand, just after finishing her exams. Finally Tom, in Perth, reckoned there would be heaps of time this arvo. None of it was difficult once I stopped working out every word and started to get the gist.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi colega de Perth dice que tendremos un montón de tiempo esta tarde.»

feedback.es: Heaps of + incontable es coloquial, típico del inglés australiano, como arvo.

origin.text: My colleague in Perth says that we will have ___ of time this arvo, so there is no need to hurry.

prompt.es: Empareja cada frase con la variedad y el significado que aporta.

feedback.es: Cada frase combina una variedad con su significado: adelantar, avisar con un toque, acabar de hacer algo y mucho tiempo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud adopta el autor ante quien dice que esas variedades son incorrectas?

choices.text: He agrees with the learners and advises avoiding such forms in exams.
He argues that each variety should be taught in schools before any standard.
He thinks the complaint overlooks how naturally language varies from one region to another.

feedback.es: El autor recuerda que cada variedad tiene reglas coherentes y se entiende entre sus hablantes: la queja nace de un malentendido; no aconseja evitarlas ni propone enseñarlas antes que el estándar.

origin.text: Some learners complain that Indian, Nigerian or Irish English is wrong. They forget that every regional variety follows its own consistent rules, and that speakers who say prepone or am after finishing are being perfectly clear to one another.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuándo debía llegar el paquete según la dependienta.

choices.text: Later that same afternoon.
Early the next morning.
Within a few days.

feedback.es: La dependienta dijo que llegaría «in the arvo», es decir, por la tarde; el comentario de la amiga sobre «heaps of time» no indica que tardara días.

origin.audio: A shop assistant in Melbourne told me that the parcel would come in the arvo. Later a friend from Sydney said that she reckoned it would take heaps of time, so I waited and made some coffee. It arrived at four.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podríamos adelantar la llamada una hora?»

feedback.es: Prepone es el verbo del inglés de la India para adelantar una cita; move también sirve, pero sin ese matiz regional.

origin.text: The call is fixed for ten, but the client is free earlier. Could we ___ the call by an hour, so that nobody has to stay late?

title.es: Lo que el hablante quiere decir

es: Deducir lo que el hablante quiere decir en diálogos cotidianos cuando la respuesta es indirecta, evasiva o muy cortés («Well… it is a bit pricey»), y leer entre líneas.

teaching.en: “Well, it is a bit pricey, so I will think about it” is a polite way of saying that the shopper will probably not buy.
teaching.es: «Bueno, es un poco caro, así que lo pensaré» es una forma cortés de decir que quien compra probablemente no comprará.
teaching.explanationEs: Dice «es caro» pero quiere decir «probablemente no»; la pausa y a bit suavizan el rechazo.
segments: “Well, it is a bit pricey, so I will think about it” is
a polite way of saying that the shopper will probably not buy.
teaching.audioText: “Well, it is a bit pricey, so I will think about it” is a polite way of saying that the shopper will probably not buy.

teaching.en: “I suppose it could work” is what people say when they accept an idea without any enthusiasm at all.
teaching.es: «Supongo que podría funcionar» es lo que se dice cuando se acepta una idea sin ningún entusiasmo.
teaching.explanationEs: I suppose suena a aceptar sin ganas: el hablante no está convencido.
segments: “I suppose it could work” is what people say when
they accept an idea without any enthusiasm at all.
teaching.audioText: “I suppose it could work” is what people say when they accept an idea without any enthusiasm at all.

teaching.en: Honest friends still try to let someone down gently, so a refusal often hides inside a compliment.
teaching.es: Los amigos sinceros también intentan rechazar con tacto, así que un rechazo suele esconderse dentro de un cumplido.
teaching.explanationEs: Let someone down gently = rechazar sin herir; el «no» se disfraza de elogio.
segments: Honest friends still try to let someone down gently,
so a refusal often hides inside a compliment.
teaching.audioText: Honest friends still try to let someone down gently, so a refusal often hides inside a compliment.

teaching.en: “It is not exactly what the client wanted, but we will see” suggests real doubt, not a promise.
teaching.es: «No es exactamente lo que quería el cliente, pero ya veremos» sugiere una duda real, no una promesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Not exactly equivale casi a «no»; we will see muestra dudas, no un compromiso.
segments: “It is not exactly what the client wanted, but
we will see” suggests real doubt, not a promise.
teaching.audioText: “It is not exactly what the client wanted, but we will see” suggests real doubt, not a promise.

teaching.en: You learn to read between the lines when someone hardly answers the question and quickly changes the subject.
teaching.es: Aprendes a leer entre líneas cuando alguien apenas responde a la pregunta y cambia rápido de tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Hardly (apenas) y un cambio de tema son señales de una respuesta evasiva.
segments: You learn to read between the lines when someone
hardly answers the question and quickly changes the subject.
teaching.audioText: You learn to read between the lines when someone hardly answers the question and quickly changes the subject.

teaching.en: Honest speakers who beat around the bush are rarely lying; to put it mildly, they just dislike saying no.
teaching.es: Quienes se andan por las ramas rara vez mienten; por decirlo suavemente, simplemente les disgusta decir que no.
teaching.explanationEs: Beat around the bush = no ir al grano; to put it mildly suaviza una crítica fuerte.
segments: Honest speakers who beat around the bush are rarely lying;
to put it mildly, they just dislike saying no.
teaching.audioText: Honest speakers who beat around the bush are rarely lying; to put it mildly, they just dislike saying no.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir realmente esta respuesta?

choices.text: She is delighted and wants to copy it.
She is not impressed but avoids saying so.
She did not notice that anything had changed.

feedback.es: La pausa y un adjetivo vago («certainly different») suavizan una opinión poco entusiasta.

hint.es: Las pausas y los adjetivos vagos suelen suavizar una crítica.

origin.text: Do you like my new coat? — Well… it is certainly different.

prompt.es: Completa: «Supongo que podría funcionar, aunque yo habría elegido otro.»

feedback.es: I suppose it could work expresa una aceptación sin entusiasmo: la frase siguiente lo confirma.

hint.es: Verbo de pensamiento que aquí significa «imagino».

origin.text: Is the new timetable acceptable? — I ___ it could work, although I would have chosen another.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada respuesta con lo que probablemente quiere decir el hablante.

pairs: Well… it is a bit pricey.

feedback.es: Cada respuesta indirecta esconde un mensaje: rechazo por el precio, un no amable, aceptación fría o falta de compromiso.

hint.es: Pregúntate qué respuesta evita decir sí o no.

pairs: Well… it is a bit pricey.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina Mia probablemente de la música.

choices.text: She loved every song the band played.
She thought the sound in the hall was poor.
She was not impressed by the music itself.

feedback.es: Mia elogia solo lo secundario (las luces y la sala) y cambia de tema: señal de que la música no la convenció; no critica el sonido de la sala, que alaba.

origin.audio: After the concert, Tom asked Mia how the band had been. She took a moment, said that the lights were lovely and the hall was very comfortable, and then asked whether they should get something to eat. Tom nodded slowly and did not ask about the singing again.

prompt.es: ¿Qué piensa realmente la autora del borrador?

choices.text: It needs substantial work before anyone outside the team sees it.
It is nearly ready and needs only small changes.
It is fine, and she only wants a second opinion first.

feedback.es: Con «I suppose», «hardly» y «let us see» suaviza una opinión clara: el borrador no está listo; no lo considera casi terminado ni pide solo una segunda opinión.

origin.text: Thanks for sending the draft. There are a few things I suppose we could look at again, and I hardly think it is ready for the client yet, but let us see how the week goes.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Supongo que podríamos intentarlo, pero no me convence.»

answer.text: I suppose we could try it but I am not convinced

feedback.es: I suppose introduce la aceptación sin ganas y but I am not convinced revela la duda real.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir Mia con «I will think about it».

choices.text: That she will buy it as soon as Tom approves the colour.
That she is probably not going to buy the lamp at all.
That she must first ask Tom to lend her the money.

feedback.es: Mia deja la lámpara en el estante y se va hacia la puerta: «I will think about it» es aquí una forma cortés de decir que probablemente no la comprará.

origin.audio: At the garden centre, Mia held up a lamp and asked Tom whether it was any good. Tom looked at the price tag and said that it was a bit pricey, but certainly bright. Outside, Tom admitted that he could hardly say he loved the colour either, and they both laughed. The assistant, who had heard everything, pretended to tidy a shelf.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y resume tres ideas y dos detalles.

answer.text: The lecturer began by saying that she wanted to look at why some companies are trying a four-day working week, and she then outlined three main reasons. According to her, the first reason is that staff are more focused when a long weekend is coming, and the work done stayed the same at one firm in Bristol. The second reason is that sick days fell sharply, by about a third in a year. The third reason is that it became easier to recruit, because candidates see the shorter week as a sign of trust. By way of illustration, she described a company that reduced its hours from forty to thirty-two without cutting pay. She went on to draw attention to a limit: the change is not suitable for every kind of business, since hospitals and shops cannot simply close on Fridays. In short, the lecturer said that the four-day week works best where results, not hours, can be measured, and she did not suggest that every company should copy it.

Firstly, staff seem to be more focused when a long weekend is coming, and at one firm in Bristol the work done did not change. Secondly, sick days fell: they went down by roughly a third in a year. Thirdly, it was easier to recruit people, since candidates see a shorter week as a sign of trust. As an example, she explained that a company cut its hours from forty to thirty-two and did not reduce pay. She also pointed out a limit: the idea does not suit every kind of business, because hospitals and shops cannot close on Fridays. To sum up, according to the lecturer, the four-day week is best where results can be measured rather than hours, although she did not say that every company should copy it.

feedback.es: El resumen recoge las tres razones, al menos dos detalles, atribuye las ideas a la conferenciante, menciona el límite y cierra con una conclusión.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y escribe un resumen con una implicación y tu reacción.

answer.text: In this episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher, whether it is better to work from home. According to the guest, it depends. First, many people save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and she called this a real benefit. Second, she said that some people feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. Third, she suggested that companies could offer two office days a week, which she described as a fair compromise. When the host asked whether working at home is better, she answered that it is not exactly better, which seemed to imply that the answer is not a simple yes. What struck me was that she never said it is easy. To be fair, I found the episode balanced, and I see her point about the benefits. However, I would add one doubt of my own: two office days a week may be hard to organise for small firms, so the compromise may suit large companies better. My gut reaction was to agree with her up to a point. In short, the episode was clear and useful, and I would like to hear how companies respond.

feedback.es: «Not exactly» es un no amable: da a entender que la respuesta no es un sí sencillo; no critica la pregunta ni afirma que el teletrabajo sea peor, porque después ofrece un compromiso.

origin.audio: In this week's episode, the host asked her guest, a researcher who studies remote work, whether working from home is better. The guest said that it depends. Many people, she explained, save about two hours a day because they no longer travel, and that is a real benefit. Asked whether it is therefore better, she answered: not exactly. Some people told her that they feel lonely and hardly see their colleagues. The host asked whether there is a solution, and the guest suggested, after a slight pause, that companies could offer two office days a week, which she called a fair compromise. She added that not everyone has a quiet room at home, a point that she said is often overlooked. The host thanked her and promised to return to the subject.

prompt.es: Completa: «Discrepo de su afirmación de que toda empresa debería permitir el teletrabajo.»

feedback.es: Take issue with + afirmación es la fórmula educada para discrepar de algo concreto.

origin.text: I agree with much of what the guest said, but I take ___ with her claim that every company should allow remote work.

prompt.es: ¿Qué impresión da la invitada, según el autor?

Careful, and honest about what her evidence could show.

feedback.es: La invitada «came across as careful rather than evasive» porque admitió lo que la investigación no podía demostrar; la impaciencia es de la presentadora, no de ella.

origin.text: The host came across as warm but slightly impatient: she thanked the guest twice, yet she interrupted the last answer to ask about the next topic. The guest, for her part, came across as careful rather than evasive, since she admitted what the research could not show.

origin.text: I liked the episode, and the guest was charming. But when the host asked about the costs to companies, the answer took four minutes and contained no number. I am not saying that she was hiding something; I am saying that I finished listening knowing less about costs than when I began.
